recipes.name: Friday Night Fish Fry
ingredients: 1 tsp Better Than Bouillon chicken paste
For the Fries and or Chips
1 cup homemade mayonnaise (or good store bought)
few drops yuzu juice or lemon juice
instructions: For the Mushy Peas
Preheat the oven to 425° F (220° C).
Combine the peas in a saucepan with water and Better than Bouillon. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2 ½ hours. - 200 g dried marrowfat peas - 500 ml water - 1 tsp Better Than Bouillon chicken paste
Place bone marrow on a rimmed baking sheet in the preheated oven and roast until brown, about 20--25 minutes depending on your oven. - 3 marrow bones
Scoop roasted marrow fat into the pot and simmer gently for 2½–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the peas break down into a thick, soft mash.
Season to taste with salt and keep warm. - salt to taste
Meanwhile, make the Fries/Chips.
For the Fries and or Chips
Optional: Use a cookie cutter to shape peeled and cut potatoes into Michelin stars.
Peel Yukon Gold potatoes and cut into thick fries. - 4 Yukon Gold potatoes
Rinse under cold water until the water runs mostly clear to remove excess starch. - cold water
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fries for 15–20 minutes, until tender but not falling apart.
Drain carefully.
Heat frying oil to 300°F (150°C). Fry potatoes in batches for 5–10 minutes, until pale and lightly cooked but not browned. - 230 ml frying oil
Remove and place on a rack to cool completely. Refrigerate or rest until fully chilled.
Meanwhile, prepare the Fish.
For the Fish
Combine kosher salt, sugar, and citrus zest. - 2 tbsp kosher salt - 2 tbsp granulated sugar - lemon zest - lime zest - orange zest
Place halibut on a wire rack over a sheet pan and lightly coat both sides with the dry brine mixture. - 4 (6 oz) Halibut loins
Refrigerate 30–60 minutes to lightly cure and season the fish
Meanwhile, make the Tartar Sauce.
For the Tartar Sauce
For the Homemade Mayonnaise
In a bowl, combine mayonnaise and crème fraîche. - 1 cup homemade mayonnaise (or good store bought) - 3 tbsp crème fraîche

Add capers, cornichons, cocktail onion, shallot, parsley, chives, dill, and marjoram. - 2 tbsp capers chopped - 5 cornichons finely chopped - 1 cocktail onion finely chopped - 1 tbsp minced shallot - 2 tbsp chopped parsley - 1 tbsp chopped chives - 1 tsp chopped dill - small pinch marjoram (optional)
Season with yuzu juice (or lemon juice) and salt to taste. - few drops yuzu juice or lemon juice - salt to taste
Mix thoroughly and refrigerate until ready to serve.
For the Batter

In a large bowl, whisk together flour, rice flour, potato starch, paprika, turmeric, baking powder, and salt. - 150 g all purpose flour - 75 g white rice flour - 75 g potato starch - ½ tsp paprika - ½ tsp turmeric - ½ tsp baking powder - ¾ tsp kosher salt
Add vodka and beer and whisk gently until a loose batter forms. Some lumps are fine. - 200 ml vodka - 226 g lager beer (about 1 cup)
For the Frying
For the Fries (Continued)
Fry the chilled potatoes again for 2–4 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp.
Remove to a rack and season immediately with salt.
For the Fish
Heat frying oil to 400°F (205°C).
Dip each halibut piece into the batter, coating completely.
Carefully lower into the hot oil and fry for 4–5 minutes, turning once, until the batter is crisp and golden and the fish is just cooked through.
Remove and drain on a rack.
For the Serving
Plate the crispy fish with a generous portion of fries.
Add a scoop of mushy peas, a side of tartar sauce, and lemon wedges. - lemon wedges
Finish with malt vinegar over the fries and fish, if desired. - malt vinegar
Serve immediately.
